shared_elements: upright pale stone slab/pillar carved in low relief
figures in profile with visible limbs/arms
horizontal band of repeated pattern dividing the surface
row of repeated similar motifs across the upper part
justification: Both are tall upright stone surfaces worked in low relief and both use a horizontal banded divider with a row of repeated motifs above it and larger creature figures below, which is the most specific correspondence. Otherwise they differ sharply: A is a dense, all-over, curvilinear composition dominated by a single frontal anthropomorphic figure with headdress and blocks of tightly packed sign-like panels, while B is sparse and schematic, with isolated animal figures floating on broad blank ground and a distinct T-shaped profile.
